# Of the Blessed Stone

...dry and moist. Therefore, that which is composed of such things is called Nature.

There are four primary qualities, namely: Heat, Dryness, Cold, and Moisture; they are called the **primary qualities** <note>original Latin: *primæ Qualitates*</note> because from them all **elements** <note>original: *Elementa*</note>, **elemental things** <term>elemental things: *elementata*; substances or bodies composed of the four basic elements, such as minerals or plants</term>, and all **temperaments** <term>temperaments: *complexiones*; the specific balance or mixture of qualities within a living body or substance</term> are composed.

### What then should an element be, and how many elements are there?

I say there are four elements: Air, Fire, Water, and Earth. A substance is called an **element**, however, because it consists of two primary qualities, and no more. Namely:

**Fire** consists of heat and dryness; **Air** of moisture and heat; **Water** of cold and moisture; and **Earth** of cold and dryness.

Within an element, these qualities are either **essential** <note>original: *essentialis*</note> or **accidental** <note>original: *accidentalis*</note>. For example: in Fire, heat is essential, while dryness is accidental. In Air, which is warm and moist, moisture is its essential quality, while heat is accidental. Water is cold and moist; here, cold is the **principal** <note>original: *principale*</note> quality, while moisture is accidental. Earth is cold and dry; here, dryness is the **essential quality** or the **principal beginning** <note>original: *essentialis Qualitas vel principale principium*</note>, and cold is accidental.

Now one must also know what an element [is...]

### What is Man and Woman, *Husband & Wife, Male & Female?*

**Socrates** in the **Assembly** <term>Assembly: The *Turba Philosophorum*, one of the oldest and most influential alchemical texts, written as a debate between ancient sages</term>: "The Woman <note>original German: *Weib*</note> is the first power of our Stone, and the Man <note>original German: *Mann*</note> is the second power of our Stone." **Socrates** (in the same place): "The secret of our Stone and Work comes from gold, and it has been formed out of Man and Woman."

Also: The **Glossary** <note>refers to a commentary or dictionary of alchemical terms</note>: "The Woman dissolves <note>original Latin: *solvit*</note> the Man, and the Man fixes <note>original German: *figiret*, meaning to make a volatile substance stable in fire</note> the Woman."

### What is one Being, *What is one thing?*

A philosopher says that it is a composition of the four elements, and is then called "one thing" <note>original Latin: *una res*</note> when the substance of the body and the water are prepared together without being divided, so that neither can be separated from the other; however, this must be done in such a way that one is volatile <note>tending to evaporate or escape when heated</note> and the other is fixed <note>stable and resistant to fire</note>.

### What is the Body, *Corpus?*

The **Glossary**: "The spirits <note>original: *Spiritus*; the volatile parts of a substance</note> do not remain in the fire if they are not mixed with the bodies <note>original: *Corporibus*</note> and, as it were, joined in fellowship; for the bodies are metals <note>original Latin: *Metalla*</note> which await the power of the fire." Therefore **Geber** <note>Jabir ibn Hayyan, an 8th-century polymath considered the father of chemistry</note> also says: "It tints <note>original: *tingiret*; to permeate and transform the color and quality of a metal</note> both bodies and spirits; the bodies are Gold and Silver."

### On the Blessed Stone

All people, both rich and poor, possess this; and without this stone, a person cannot live. Both the **perfect and imperfect bodies** <note>original Latin: *Corpora perfecta & imperfecta*; in alchemy, "perfect" bodies refer to gold and silver, while "imperfect" bodies are base metals like lead, tin, or copper.</note> contain it, and it is well known that no metal can exist without **quicksilver** <note>original Latin: *Arg. viv.* (Argentum vivum), literally "living silver."</note>.

Our Stone is born upon two mountains; therefore a **philosopher** <note>original Latin: *Philosophus*; a term commonly used to refer to an alchemist or a sage of the natural arts.</note> says:

> My son, go to the highest mountains in India, and take from them beautiful stones, **honored stones** <note>original Latin: *Lapides honoratos*.</note>. To those highest mountains, to make perfect **metals** <note>original Latin: *Metalla*.</note>.

Our Stone is also called an **animal** <note>original Latin: *Animal*.</note>, a creature, because just as a creature has in and of itself body, soul, and spirit—**because just as an animal has in itself body, spirit, and soul** <note>original Latin: *pro eo, quod sicut Animal in se habet Corpus, Spiritum & Animam*.</note>—and it is accustomed to rest in the fire with perfect bodies.

->Now follows: of how many kinds is the **Philosophers’ Stone**?<- <note>original Latin: *Lapis Philosophorum*.</note>

The **Philosophers’ Stone** is of three kinds in terms of words: namely, in **body, spirit, and soul** <note>original Latin: *Corpore, Spiritu & Anima*.</note>. And it is of two kinds in **species or substance** <note>original Latin: *spec. vel substantia*.</note>; one is of the body, and so forth. However, they differ **by reason of definition, according to Aristotle** <note>original Latin: *ratione Definitionis, secundum Aristotelem*. Aristotle's theories on the composition of matter were the framework for medieval alchemy.</note>, for nothing causes more confusion and errors than the multiplicity of names.

->Here ends the treatise of Mr. **Bernard of Treviso**, **Canon of Regensburg**<- <note>original Latin: *Bernhardi Treverensis, Canonici Ratisponentium*. Bernard of Treviso was a 15th-century alchemist famous for his long search for the Stone; "Canon of Regensburg" identifies him with the ecclesiastical office he was traditionally said to hold.</note>.

In such a way works the <term>elixir</term> <note>In alchemy, the elixir is the refined substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold or granting longevity</note> which is sought; for experience (or rather, experience shows it) destroys the form <note>original Latin: *destruirt formam*</note> and introduces a new specific one <note>original Latin: *introducirt specificativam novam*</note>.

Now that the elements <note>original Latin: *Elementa*</note> are divided, it seems that nothing of them is touched except earth and water, air and fire, but not their powers, nor are they known except in the primary elements <note>original Latin: *nec scientur nisi in prioribus elementis*</note>.

Air and fire are indeed **rare** <note>original German: *rara*; meaning thin, subtle, or lacking density</note> (thin, diluted, very delicate) and certainly **simple** <note>original Latin: *simplicia*; fundamental substances that cannot be further divided</note>; therefore they cannot be seen with the eyes at all.

Nevertheless, there are four elements, four modes, and four <term>humors</term> <note>The "humors" were the four vital fluids of ancient and medieval medicine—blood, yellow bile, phlegm, and black bile—believed to regulate health and personality</note>, namely blood, bile, watery moisture, and melancholy (Latin: *Sangvis, Cholera, Phlegma, & Melancholia*).

The modes are: Hot, Cold, Moist, and Dry <note>original Latin: *Calidum, Frigidum, Humidum, & Siccum*</note>.

At this point, doubt is cast upon the <term>Philosophers’ Stone</term> <note>the legendary alchemical substance capable of turning base metals into gold or producing the Elixir of Life</note>—concerning what it is and what its nature might be—which has never been openly named by any <term>Philosopher</term> <note>in this context, an alchemist or natural scientist</note>, nor is it named now. We have, however, reserved for ourselves the duty to teach this sincerely.

The writings of the Sages show that it is one single thing, and nothing else should be *joined* <note>original Latin-German: *conjungiret*</note> with it, because nothing suits a thing or agrees with it except that which is closest to its nature; for every thing brings forth its own kind, as is also seen in fruits.

Therefore, when things from one *genus* <note>class or category</note> have the same *roots* <note>original Latin: *radices*</note>, they are also one. But if they are different, they also produce different things.

Recognize, therefore, and distinguish the pure from the impure; that which has nothing can give nothing.

The pure is of a single essence, free from all *alterations* <note>original Latin: *Alterationibus*</note> or changes. The impure, however, is united and mixed with various *contrary* <note>original German-Latin: *contrairen*</note> parts, and is therefore very easily *corrupted* <note>original German-Latin: *corrumpiret*</note> and spoiled.

# Of the Blessed Stone

<note>The text begins mid-sentence, likely completing a word like "frigiditas" from the previous page.</note> [fri]gidity, or coldness, is missing; whereas warmth is missing from tin and lead.

Gold has held its value from the beginning of the world and has been highly esteemed, held in higher regard than all <term>metals</term> and <term>minerals</term>, because it is the <term>ferment of the Elixir</term> <note>original Latin: *fermentum Elixir*; just as yeast causes bread to rise, this "ferment" is the essential catalyst that triggers the alchemical transformation of base metals into gold</note>, without which nothing in our Work can be accomplished.

It is like a ferment in dough, like <term>rennet</term> <note>original: *gelöberte Milch*; the substance used to curdle milk</note> or <term>coagulated</term> <note>original: *coagulirte*; thickened or solidified from a liquid state</note> milk in cheese, and like musk among spices. Therefore, if I do not see the <term>Sun</term> <note>original: *Solem*; in alchemy, the Sun is the symbol for gold</note>, then I say for certain that the <term>Mastery</term> <note>original: *Magisterium*; the successful completion of the alchemical process</note> is not true or correct, for every thing increases after its own kind. Gold is a <term>tincture</term> <note>original: *Tinctur*; a substance capable of deeply penetrating and changing the color and nature of another material</note> of redness, or gives a red tincture, which transforms every <term>Body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*; the physical substance of a base metal</note>. Silver, however, is a tincture of whiteness, or gives a white tincture, because she is a ruler of moisture—namely, the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: *Luna*; the alchemical symbol for silver</note>.

# Of the Sages

And so it is with all things that differ in **Matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note>.

Therefore, it is well to note that the **Agent** <note>The active force or "doer"</note> is also the **Patient** <note>original: *Patiens*; the passive receiver or the one acted upon</note>; thus, a thing which exists in **Genus** <note>original: *in genere*; the general category</note> also exists in **Species** <note>original: *in specie*; the specific type</note>.

They must be one in one, and not something else, diverse or contrary, if it is to be multiplied and increased—indeed, if anything worthy is to come of it.

A human begets a human, an animal begets an animal, even in the **Vegetable Kingdom** <note>original: *Regno vegetabili*</note>, a pear tree begets a pear tree naturally, and pears; an apple tree begets an apple tree, and so forth.

It must also be considered that, although they come together as one, it is still a **distinct operation, as is fitting between the agent and the patient** <note>original: *Operatio distincta, ut convenit inter agentem & patientem*</note>.

The **Matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note> undergoes the **Action**, but the **Form** <note>original: *Forma*; the organizing principle or essence</note> acts in such a way that it joins the Matter to itself and, as it were, makes the Matter like itself.

Thus, by nature, Matter desires **Form**, just as the woman desires the man, and **the base desires the honorable** <note>original: *turpe honestum*; a classical philosophical maxim meaning the imperfect seeks the perfect, or the ugly seeks the beautiful</note>.

In the same way, the **Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> gladly and willingly embraces the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> by nature, so that the body may reach its perfection.

Therefore, learn to recognize the **Mineral Roots** <note>original: *Radices minerales*</note>—the origins or the beginning of those minerals—and you shall perform your work accordingly.

# Of the Blessed Stone

...not through mere naming or expression, but through a description and circumscription of its origins <note>original: *suarum radicum*; literally "its roots"</note>, and done openly, without concealment.

## Of the Blessed Stone

...the whole **Work** <term>Work: Often called the "Great Work" (Magnum Opus), this is the entire process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term> is completed. And it is indeed a **flask** <note>German: *Kolbe*</note>, and a single **helm** <note>German: *Helm*; the cooling cap of a still or alembic that fits over the flask</note>, and a glass vessel which is so firm and strong, sealed on all sides, an ell <term>Ell: A historical unit of measurement, roughly the length of a man's arm (approx. 24–45 inches).</term> long, round, pure and smooth, and wide enough, the bottom of which should be slightly curved or bent, about the size of a head at the sides, so that the **sublimation** <term>Sublimation: In alchemy, the process where a substance is heated into vapor and then condensed back into a solid, used to purify the matter.</term> can rise and descend all the better and more freely; the fire should be above and below, as necessity requires, so that it can be lit all the better.

The glass must be thus, namely strong and clear, so that one may see the **Work**, translucent, and yet well-sealed, so that nothing of the **spirit** <note>original: *Spiritu*</note> may pass through or escape; it must be so firm that the volatile **spirits** <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> can be held and not driven away by the fire, so that the appearing colors in the **Work** are not hindered by any excess of heat from the fire.

Especially for this reason: because some **bodies** <note>original: *Corpora*</note> are shadowy <note>original: *schatticht*; likely meaning opaque or dense</note> and others are porous, and thus the **spirits** gradually escape as a vapor or smoke.

And because the volatile **spirits** rise and do not descend, the **helm** must be properly fitted into the **flask**, so that the **joints** <note>original: *Juncturen*</note> are well-fitted and join together closely, so that nothing can come out or in; for if air or moisture were to enter, the **Work** would be ruined.

# On the Blessed Stone

And its Father is the Sun <note>original: *Sol*; represents the active, masculine principle or gold</note>, its Mother is the Moon <note>original: *Luna*; represents the passive, feminine principle or silver</note>; the Wind <note>original: *Ventus*</note> carried it in its belly, and the Earth <note>original: *Terra*</note> was deprived of it <note>The text here adapts the *Tabula Smaragdina* (Emerald Tablet), a foundational hermetic text</note>, because you have received the Water from the Air, the Air from the Fire, and the Fire from the Earth by distilling them.

Through the frequent repetition of **sublimation** <term>Sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it turns into vapor and then solidifies again, used here to purify the material</term>, the **soul** <note>original: *Anima*</note>, which rises with the water, is purified; and the coarseness or thickness, **descending to the bottom** <note>original: *ad ima descendens*</note>, **becomes moon-like** <note>original: *lunatur*; refers to the substance becoming bright, white, or silver-colored</note> and becomes light.

The **heat** <note>original: *Calidum*</note> is mixed with the moisture, and the dryness with the cold. In such a way, you shall perform the mixing.

Since one cannot come from one extreme to another except through a **medium** <note>In alchemy, a "medium" is a middle substance or state that bridges two opposites, such as air acting as a bridge between fire and water</note>.

Therefore, take the **submerged flying volatile** <term>Volatile Volans submersum: A spirit that is naturally inclined to evaporate (fly) but has been successfully trapped or "submerged" in a solid body.</term>, surrender it, and bring it to the point where it must answer you in the landscapes <note>Possibly referring to the visual patterns that form inside the alchemical glass.</note> without fleeing, and must come to you; for that which is below is as that which is above, and that which is above is as that which is below. **For, that which is lower is like that which is higher, and that which is higher is like that which is lower.** <note>original Latin: "nam, qvod est inferius, est sicut qvod est superius, & qvod est superius, est sicut qvod est inferius." This is the famous central axiom of the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, expressing the correspondence between the microcosm and macrocosm.</note>

For this reason, our blessed water comes to water its earth, to [cleanse] the blackness...

### ARNOLD OF VILLANOVA in THE GREAT ART.
->*Here begins the Work of the Magnificent Master Arnold of Villanova, in the Great Art.*<-

The matter of our Stone is a thing of little value; it is to be found everywhere, because it is a slimy water <note>original Latin: "Aqua viscosa"</note>, and yet it is <term>Living silver: Also known as quicksilver or mercury.</term> <note>original Latin: "Argent. viv."</note> because it is drawn from the earth with friendliness. Various ancients have said that such matter is found everywhere; and various people who did not understand it sought it in raw filth and dung. # Of the Blessed Stone

Thus the *Quintessence* <term>Quintessence: Literally the "fifth essence," the purest and most concentrated substance or spirit extracted from a material through alchemical processes.</term>, which is the *Spirit of Mercury*, is extracted from the air, and indeed in the following manner:

Take 1 pound <note>original: "℞. ℔ j." — ℞ is the standard apothecary symbol for "take," and ℔ represents a pound weight.</note> of *Saltpeter* <term>Saltpeter: Potassium nitrate, used in alchemy as a powerful oxidizing agent and a key ingredient in making strong acids.</term> and as much *Vitriol* <term>Vitriol: Metallic sulfates, used here to produce corrosive vapors when heated with saltpeter.</term>, make an *Aqua Fortis* <term>Aqua Fortis: Literally "strong water," or nitric acid, used to dissolve metals.</term>, and finely grind the aforementioned *Mercury*, and *dissolve* it in warm ashes <note>Warm ashes provided a steady, gentle heat for the glass vessel.</note> in such water, in a sealed glass for twelve hours; and if it does not *dissolve*, then add a seventh part of well-ground *Sal Ammoniac* <term>Sal Ammoniac: Ammonium chloride, often used to help dissolve substances that nitric acid alone could not, creating a version of "Aqua Regia."</term> to it, in *relation* to the water or a little more. This is a great secret, which you may keep to yourself.

After this has happened, *distill* an *Aqua Fortis* and save it; provide an even stronger fire, so that the *Mercury* rises up the sides of the glass, and this is the *Quintessence of Mercury* <note>original Latin: "Qv. Ess. Mercurii"</note>, whiter than snow.

Strengthen the fire even more, so that the entire, full *Spirit* will rise upward; thus the *Quintessence* is extracted, and at the bottom will remain black and burnt dregs, *from the sublimated Spirit of Mercury* <note>original Latin: "à Spiritu Mercurii sublimati"</note>.

Note that in this operation you have accomplished two things which you did not know before, and which were previously quite imperfect, as it completely burned the *Aqua Fortis*; it is very wondrous that that which was as white as snow extracted from itself that black *earthiness* <term>Terrestrität: Earthiness or dross; the impure, heavy material that is separated from the pure spirit during distillation.</term>.

### Dearest Friend.

I would have heartfully wished to have answered long ago and given my opinion <note>original: "Sentiment"</note>, as requested, regarding the Hermetic Federation <note>original: "Foederatis Hermeticis"</note> and their so-called *Second Trumpet-Blast Epistle* <note>original: "Epistola Buccinatoria secunda" — a manifesto intended to announce alchemical discoveries.</note>; had my many affairs at that time not prevented it. # Of the Sages.

This second Trumpet-Blast Epistle <note>original: "Epistola Buccinatoria"</note>, which was dedicated and offered to me and to Johannes de Monte Hermetis <note>A pseudonym likely meaning "John of the Hermetic Mountain."</note>. When I read it through, I found the very same twelve questions that I had posed to the Rosicrucians <term>Rosen-Creußer</term> <note>A secret brotherhood of alchemists and mystics active in the 17th century.</note>, which they have made somewhat more long-winded. However, I find in these accounts of theirs neither substance nor strength <note>original: "Safft noch Krafft"</note>, and not even a tiny spark appears from which I could discern the title of "True Hermetic Sages," with which they have boasted so much in order to gain a reputation.

I will allow them to pass as learned, well-read men experienced in many languages; however, I would not wish to speak to their disgrace by saying they had achieved much in Natural Philosophy <term>Philosophia naturali</term> <note>The study of nature and the physical universe, the precursor to modern science.</note>.

And although I truly do not envy anyone the Hermetic name <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note>, nor do I begrudge its prestige, I still do not believe that they will ever attain it, nor that they will extract the secrets of Hermetic Philosophy <term>Philosophiam Hermeticam</term>, especially since they do not even understand the Emerald Tablet <term>Tabulam Smaragdina</term> <note>A foundational, cryptic Alchemical text said to contain the secrets of the "prima materia" and the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. In the beginning of the Trumpet-Blast Epistle, I see no particular secret <term>Arcanum</term>; that they, like others, are entirely ignorant of the principles of nature <term>Principia naturae</term>, I cannot deny. I believe, however, that those who go about "heavy with child" with their wisdom will give birth to a magnificent wind <note>A metaphorical way of saying their great efforts will result in nothing but empty air.</note>. That they are distinguished and respectable people, I well believe; but that they have also labored so fruitlessly through the whole night—they are truly worthy of pity.

# Of the Blessed Stone

What would it matter to us if one or more among us, through the grace of God, possessed this noble treasure—namely the **Philosopher’s Stone** <term>Stein der Weisen</term> <note>The legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>, for which the **Two Men** <term>Duum-Viri</term> <note>A Latin term for a committee of two people; here referring to the leaders of the rival Hermetic group.</note> strive so terribly—and whether all of them, or just a few, should they fail to reach their goal, would either give up everything out of impatience or misfortune, or, still hoping, venture one last attempt? # On the Blessed Stone

...would find these **opinions** <term>opiniones</term> <note>Referring to the conflicting views of alchemists mentioned on the previous page.</note> notable based on my own example.

When I was staying in the **East Indies** <term>India Orientali</term> in the year 1678, I published the **Introduction to a True and Unheard-of Physics** <note>original: "Introitum ad veram & inauditam Physicam"; this refers to Hellwig's own 1678 treatise on physical and alchemical observations.</note>. Regarding the other letter, however, we were to report how your noble name was only recently mentioned in it; we therefore most humbly ask that you do not misinterpret our good intentions, and that you might devote a little time to reading through both. ### *The Printer to the Reader!* <note>original: *Typographus ad Lectorem!*</note>
